name: Dumbbell Bench Press
summary: A flat pressing movement with dumbbells that allows a deeper stretch and a more natural arm path than the barbell version, while training each side independently.
setup: Sit on the end of a flat bench with the dumbbells resting on your thighs.
Lie back, kicking the dumbbells up to chest level one at a time or together.
Pull shoulder blades back and down, feet planted on the floor.
Press the dumbbells above the chest with palms facing forward or slightly angled in.
execution: Lower the dumbbells under control to the sides of the chest with elbows about 45-70 degrees from the torso.
Stop when the upper arms are around parallel to the floor or you feel a comfortable chest stretch.
Press up and slightly inward until the arms are straight, without clanking the dumbbells hard together.
Return the dumbbells to your thighs and sit up carefully when finished.
cues: Squeeze the chest as you press
mistakes: Elbows flared out wide: angle them in toward 45-70 degrees.
Going too heavy and losing control: choose a weight you can lower for a 2-3 second count.
Lowering too deep so shoulders roll forward: stop at a comfortable stretch.
Hips lifting or back over-arching: keep glutes on the bench and feet planted.
